figures.sourceContext: Section 9.2 Definition 3 defines convexity by containing every straight segment between two points. Proposition 8 shows connected open subsets of R^n are polygonally connected.
facts: An actual three-dimensional open product box contains both Euclidean vectors and the complete interpolated segment. The affine wireframe display preserves the original dashed rear edge, segment overlap and x/y labels.
limits: The generic source cube does not prescribe coordinates; representative strictly interior vectors are factual metadata, while perspective is Style geometry.

figures.sourceContext: Section 9.2 Proposition 8 begins with fixed u and the polygonally reachable set A. A local basic product neighborhood V of a permits extending the route by a straight segment.
facts: Connected open U, reachable set A, Convex(V), V subset U, the original route u to a and its one-segment extension to b are explicit. Source labels are u,a,V,U, with the extension dot unlabeled.
limits: Printed page 191 is absent. The supplied statement and opening proof plus the visible sketch are used; absent prose is not reconstructed.
The irregular open U is a generic illustrative contour in Style. All rendered route vertices and both local endpoints are independently checked inside the contour and V.

figures.sourceContext: Section 9.3 Example 8 defines S by x²+y²<1 and T by (x−2)²+y²<1. ClS intersects T and S intersects ClT trivially, while ClS intersects ClT nontrivially.
facts: The contact point (1,0) belongs to both closed disks and neither open disk. Opposite source hatch directions, center dots, coordinate axes and source knockouts are retained.
limits: Boundary circles are not added to the hatch-only source drawing. Subdued orange fill is the consistent permitted color addition.

figures.sourceContext: Section 9.3 Example 10 considers r=1−1/λ, λ>1 in polar coordinates, then adjoins limit-circle points.
facts: The exact reciprocal spiral is a continuous connected image of λ>1. The true closure includes both the unit circle and the omitted initial origin; a source-like native topological spiral display uses a strictly increasing radial chart.
limits: The printed equation ClY=Y union {r=1} omits the origin limit as λ tends to 1 from above. Substance keeps that mathematical endpoint; the source graphic and label 0 are preserved.

Canonical Style uses the strictly increasing fourth-power odds radial display q(r)=r^4/(r^4+5000(1−r)^4) on normalized radii, with finite endParameter=10π. This is a topological sketch whose radial display is not metric. radialPower=1 gives the identity metric view; an explicit other radialPower selects a power chart. The default chart fixes zero and the unit-circle limit and preserves strict radial order. Exact source coil spacing remains approximate.
The infinite tail is represented by a finite phase window and the dashed limiting circle; no circle membership is inferred from drawing adjacency.

figures.sourceContext: Section 9.4 Proposition 12 proves a product is connected iff each factor is connected; the two-factor argument assumes a separation U,V and uses horizontal/vertical connected slices through u and v.
facts: The alleged separation is nested in Hypothesis. W is a genuine product box containing u, W subset U. A1=R×{u2} and A2={v1}×R meet at (v1,u2), joining u to v.
limits: U/V labels in the source identify the assumed separation, not literal geometric half-planes. No connected plane is asserted to have an actual separation.
Source labels are (u1,u2),(v1,v2),A1,A2,W1×W2,U,V and (0,0); the shared point is factual and is not drawn as an extra labeled dot.

figures.sourceContext: Section 9.5 Example 17 has Cn={(x,y):x²+y²=(1−1/n)²} and the two horizontal lines. These are separate components, although the space cannot be split between (0,1) and (0,−1).
facts: Disconnected induced topology, ComponentOf each circle and both lines, and CannotSplitBetween the upper/lower points are distinct explicit statements. C1 is the radius-zero singleton.
limits: Finite circles n=2,3,4,5,6,8,12,20 represent the infinite accumulating family; C1 is the origin. The dashed unit circle is an accumulation annotation, not an asserted subset of Y.
The source is disconnected. Earlier inventory shorthand calling it connected is superseded by this source-verified review.

figures.sourceContext: Section 9.5 Proposition 18: a reverse-inclusion-directed family of closed subsets of compact Hausdorff X, each unsplittable between x,y, has an intersection likewise unsplittable. The proof supposes a split of B and uses disjoint ambient neighborhoods G,H.
facts: Compact T2 premises, directed closed family, intersection B and unsplittable conclusion are explicit. SplitBetween(B,x,y,U,V,tau) is nested in Hypothesis; disjoint G/H enclose U/V, and a selected xi lies in Ai outside G union H.
limits: Both B labels refer to the same intersection, with U,V shown in the conditional contradiction branch. Derived branch facts are schematic proof context, not an unconditional true separation.
The source has labels Ai,U,V,G,H,B,B,xi, without a/b dots. The xi dot is independently checked inside the native Ai contour and outside both G/H contours.
